_comment: Access policy enforced by hooks/policy-gate.sh (PreToolUse on Write|Edit|NotebookEdit|Bash).
LAW 2: gates fail closed. If this file is unreadable or malformed, writes under
fallback_protected are DENIED and everything else is allowed - a broken policy can
neither expose the protected tree nor brick the session.
Identity comes from the hook payload's agent_type/agent_name; absent identity means the
main session (the orchestrator), which is trusted for the protected tree.
record_root: leave null for the sibling default <parent>/<repo>_claude_iff. The gate and
the tools both resolve it through _lib.record_root(), so the deny rule can never point
somewhere different from where capture actually writes.
_protected_comment: Every directory whose contents the gate itself executes or trusts. tools/ is here because
policy_gate.py imports _lib from it on every tool call: a sub-agent that can write
.claude/tools/_lib.py owns the gate on the very next call. skills/ and console/ are here
for the same reason, one step removed.

derived_files._comment: Regenerated by the ritual; hand edits are lost on the next build. Warned about, not denied - a human debugging the console must be able to poke at it.

_comment: Applies to any sub-agent identity not named below. The main session is never subject to
this block: only an explicit agents.orchestrator entry can restrict the orchestrator.
deny_bash names commands sub-agents may not run. read_only_subcommands carves out the
harmless half: a verifier that cannot run `git log` cannot verify a claim about history,
while `git push` stays the main session's job. Deny the mutation, not the noun.
_read_only_comment: Subcommands that cannot mutate, whatever flags follow. branch, tag and remote are NOT
here on purpose: `git branch -D`, `git tag -d` and `git remote set-url` all destroy or
redirect. Neither is symbolic-ref: its two-argument form WRITES the ref;
`rev-parse --symbolic-full-name` covers the read use. Allowlist read-only OPERATIONS,
never nouns that happen to have a read-only spelling.

_comment: skills/ is granted because implementing an approved evolution change with the smallest
primitive often means writing a skill. hooks/, config/, agents/ and protocols/ are NOT
granted: the anatomist proposes those and the main session applies them.

retro-analyst._comment: Propose-only by tool restriction in its agent file; no write grants here either.
